_about: Recurring political-interest and political-representation questions from the Australian Election Study's national post-election surveys. Campaign-news channels, political participation and one-off election questions are outside this store.
_readme: Generated by .build/extract-aes-interest.py from the ADA general release of the Australian Election Study integrated file 1967–2025 v1 (2_aes67to25_integrated_general_v1.dta), whose respondent data is licensed and not committed. Question wording is quoted from the 2025 questionnaire (A1/A3/C6/C8). Figures were cross-checked against the AES's official Trends in Australian Political Opinion 1987–2025 (November 2025): Interest in the election, p10; Interest in politics, p74; Who the government is run for, p104; Politicians know what ordinary people think, p107. The 1993 and 2010–2025 waves are weighted to the national electorate; 1987/1990 and 1996–2007 are unweighted in this release. Percentages are weighted response distributions at one decimal, not reverse-engineered from the report's rounded charts. Wave dates use the month after polling day, matching data/trust-government.json's AES convention.

entries.question: Generally speaking, how much interest do you usually have in what's going on in politics?
entries.notes: The 2025 questionnaire's wording (A1); integrated-file variable polintr. Unweighted in the integrated release; shares are of valid answers, with missing, skipped and zero-weight rows excluded. SampleEff is Kish's effective sample from the release weight. Wave dated to the month after polling day.
